skill.name: nature-experiment-log
skill.description: Converts experiment images, notes, transcripts, and local files into structured Markdown logs with traceable attachments and optional Obsidian or Feishu integration.
skill.summary: Create consistent, traceable experiment records from mixed laboratory source material.

content.value_statement: Scattered laboratory notes make experiments difficult to review and reproduce. This skill organizes mixed source material into structured Markdown records with linked attachments.
actual_capabilities: Organizes uploaded images, transcripts, text, and local files into experiment records.
Produces Markdown logs with YAML frontmatter and consistent experiment identifiers.
Lists missing or ambiguous details for user confirmation instead of inventing values.
Links logs to archived source images, audio, tables, and message attachments.
Supports optional Obsidian indexes and Feishu message retrieval workflows.
limitations: It cannot verify scientific accuracy beyond the supplied source material.
It does not infer missing temperatures, durations, recipes, devices, or results.
Feishu retrieval requires a configured bot, suitable permissions, and the separate CLI integration.
Obsidian dashboards require the Dataview plugin and correctly placed template files.

use_cases.title: Record Daily Bench Work
use_cases.description: Turn notes, photographs, and voice transcripts into a consistent daily experiment log.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Records
use_cases.description: Apply shared identifiers, fields, attachment paths, and missing-data checks across a project.

use_cases.title: Build a Searchable Archive
use_cases.description: Create Markdown records and optional Obsidian indexes for reviewing experiments and anomalies.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Log
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an experiment log from these notes. Preserve unknown values as confirmation items and return save-ready Markdown.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has a short set of typed observations.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Mixed Materials
prompt_templates.prompt: Organize these images, transcripts, and notes into one experiment record. List each source attachment and identify missing fields.
prompt_templates.scenario: Several source formats describe one experiment.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Project Naming
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a structured log using project code [CODE], sample batch [BATCH], and output root [PATH]. Follow the documented experiment ID rules.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs consistent identifiers and storage paths.

prompt_templates.title: Update the Research Archive
prompt_templates.prompt: Build the experiment log from the supplied materials, archive attachments, update the experiment index, and append any anomaly. Confirm ambiguous facts before writing.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced workflow maintains linked logs, indexes, and anomaly records.

output_examples.input: 316L sample, 500 C chloride corrosion for 300 hours in argon, with 0.0032 g mass loss.
output_examples.output: A Markdown experiment log with identifiers, conditions, observations, results, missing-field questions, and an attachment section.

output_examples.input: Three furnace photographs and a voice transcript describing a thermal stability test.
output: A structured thermal stability record with YAML metadata.
An attachment index describing each photograph and transcript.
A confirmation list for uncertain temperatures, timings, or sample identifiers.

output_examples.input: Create an Obsidian record and note that the temperature controller drifted during the run.
output_examples.output: A linked experiment note, an anomaly entry for the controller drift, and an updated index-ready record.

best_practices: Provide dates, sample identifiers, conditions, observations, and source attachments together.
Review every confirmation item before treating the generated record as final.
Choose the output directory and naming conventions before requesting file creation.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to invent missing measurements or scientific conclusions.
Do not grant Feishu or filesystem access beyond the required project scope.
Do not overwrite established experiment identifiers without checking linked records.

faq.question: Which source materials can I provide?
faq.answer: You can provide text, images, audio, voice transcripts, instrument screenshots, local files, or folders.

faq.question: Does the skill require Obsidian?
faq.answer: No. It can return or save standard Markdown without Obsidian.

faq.question: Does the skill require Feishu?
faq.answer: No. Feishu is optional and only supports retrieving authorized group messages and attachments.

faq.question: How are missing details handled?
faq.answer: Missing or ambiguous facts are listed for confirmation and are not invented.

faq.question: Can it update experiment indexes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes templates for an Obsidian Dataview index, anomaly log, and equipment tracking.

faq.question: Does it validate experimental conclusions?
faq.answer: No. It structures supplied information but does not independently verify scientific claims or measurements.
